color_contrast_surface_label: Example State official voter-information color, contrast, and non-color cue fail-open policy
delivery_role_note: Critical official voter-information routes remain readable and interpretable without relying on faint contrast or color alone to convey status, urgency, selection, or required action.
text_contrast_note: Critical answer/help text stays readable against its background without faint low-emphasis styling carrying the current answer.
non_text_contrast_note: Controls, icons, markers, state pills, and other graphics needed to understand or act on the answer remain visually distinguishable from adjacent colors.
non_color_cue_note: Required, selected, urgent, corrective, and unavailable states use a visible cue beyond hue alone, such as text labels, shapes, icons, grouping, or patterns.
status_and_priority_cue_note: Warnings, deadlines, and current-state labels remain noticeable under ordinary glare, grayscale, or low-brightness conditions.
action_affordance_visibility_note: Links, buttons, and next-action affordances remain visibly actionable rather than blending into surrounding content.
graphic_legend_and_map_cue_note: Legends, charts, and map/list markers required to understand the answer include text or other redundant cues instead of color-only distinctions.
same_answer_across_visual_variants_note: High-contrast themes, grayscale rendering, or other visual variants may change styling but do not silently change the authoritative answer.
manual_help_contact_note: A plainly visible first-party help/contact lane remains available when the main route becomes visually ambiguous.
